sub.en: Look at what comes just BEFORE each infinitive — a noun, an adjective, or a verb?

acts.title: What the job actually involves now
text: Ask somebody what their job is and they will name a profession. Ask what it involves and you get something quite different, and usually longer.

An advertising director described his week to us like this: “My job is to advise clients about their campaigns. In practice, my job is to attend five or six meetings a day, to give presentations at most of them, and to entertain clients in the evening. The advising takes about four hours a week.”

The gap between the title and the work has widened since offices emptied. Remote work removed the corridor conversation, and the corridor conversation was where about a third of the coordinating used to happen. It has been replaced by more meetings, which is why people who work from home often report longer days and higher productivity at the same time. Both things are true.

Hybrid arrangements have their own problem: it is important to decide which days, and to decide them for the team rather than the person. A team where everybody chooses freely is a team that is never in the same room.
The honest summary is that a job now involves more explaining and less doing than it did ten years ago. Whether that is progress depends entirely on how much you like meetings.

items.q: The four words that introduce what the job involves.
The three words used before an infinitive to say something matters.
The preposition used before “offices emptied”.
The word for working two days in the office and three at home.

use: I spend a lot of time…
tts: I work for an advertising agency. I’m a director and my job is to advise clients about their advertising campaigns.
I spend a lot of time in meetings — I attend five or six meetings a day, sometimes more. And they’re usually at the clients’ offices, not at my own, unfortunately.
I often have to give presentations at the meetings, so it can be quite stressful. I also entertain clients a lot — you know, take them to restaurants.

write.q: Describe what your job or your studies actually involve: 6 sentences. Use “My job is to…”, “It’s important to…”, “I have to…” and “I find it hard to…”, plus one verb that takes -ing instead.
write.model: My job is to prepare the weekly figures for four regions and to explain them to people who do not read them. It’s important to send them on Monday morning, because everything else that week depends on that one file. I have to attend three meetings I do not need to be in, and I have stopped pretending otherwise. I find it hard to say no to extra work, which is a problem I have had since university. I enjoy building the templates far more than I enjoy the meetings. If I could change one thing, it would be the meetings.

speak.q: Answer out loud: What is your job, and what does it involve? What is it important to do in your work? What do you have to do that you would rather not? What do you find hard?
speak.model: My job is to prepare the weekly figures and explain them. It’s important to send them on Monday. I have to go to three meetings I don’t need. I find it hard to say no to extra work.
